summary: The one-line production change is correct and complete for the collision it was filed to close: after it, no acquisition path can yield epoch 0 (cold start writes 1; takeover is current+1 and Lease refuses a negative epoch; renew/release keep the held epoch), so every leased chain is disjoint from the unleased epoch-0 chain. Request counts are byte-identical -- one stat plus one conditional PUT per acquisition, nothing added, nothing in a loop, nothing scaling with records, shards, partitions or indices. The Test-removed: trailer is the right instrument for the rename, not the inversion testing.md rule 4 exists to catch. One major: the diff hands M4.5/M4.6 a wiring that is NOT 'straight in' -- reserving 0 converts a shared-chain safety bug into a permanently forked, unsealable epoch-0 chain that a leased reader never reads, and DefaultIngest is still the production writer on it. Nothing in the tree owns that constraint, and the staged backlog row says the opposite.

findings.title: Reserving 0 makes the epoch-0 chain unreadable AND unsealable, and nothing owns removing its production writer before the wiring
findings.failure_scenario: The staged row asserts 'M4.5 and M4.6 can now wire lease.epoch() straight in', and CommitLog's new javadoc presents the epoch-0 chain as a steady state ('what every call site that has no lease yet still writes'). Take that at face value at M4.6: change DefaultIngest:135 to new CommitLog(store, prefix, lease.epoch()) on the pod that holds the lease and leave the other pods on the 2-arg constructor. recover() (CommitLog.java:110) lists logPrefix() for its OWN epoch only and nextOffset() defaults to 0 for an unseen RunKey, so the first leader at epoch 1 recovers nothing from the epoch-0 chain and re-issues offsets that chain already assigned -- two records at offset 0 for one stream -- while the unleased pods keep committing into a chain no leased reader ever lists. Their records are acked and never become visible: silent loss, not a stall. Worse, that chain cannot be closed by M4.6's seal protocol: sealing depends on a losing writer treating its loss at N+1 as proof it is fenced and STOPPING, and an unleased CommitLog.commit does the opposite by design (on a lost putIfAbsent it reads the winner, folds the offsets in and retries N+2, forever, CommitLog.java:170-176). The epoch-0 chain has no leader to fence, so I3's sealed-prefix clause is unsatisfiable for the 0->1 transition. Before this change a first leader shared that chain -- unsafe, but continuous; after it the two forks are provably disjoint, which is exactly the property that makes the fork silent. The reservation is still the right call, but its cost is an obligation this diff does not record anywhere: the wiring commit must ELIMINATE the unleased production commit path (DefaultIngest acquires or forwards), not merely pass an epoch, and M4.5's CONTINUE cannot use prevEpoch=0 as a 'no previous chain' sentinel now that 0 names a real, live chain. Fix is one sentence: state it on the M4.5 and/or M4.6 rows (both todo) and in CommitLog's 2-arg javadoc, or file it as its own row the way M4.4 filed this one.
findings.suggestion: Add to the M4.5/M4.6 rows: once any writer uses a leased epoch, every production commit path must be leased -- the epoch-0 chain is unreadable by a leased reader and unsealable, because its writers never stop on a lost race. And note that prevEpoch=0 in CONTINUE means the unleased chain, never 'none'.

findings.title: The record that defines the epoch still documents the opposite of the reservation, and does not enforce it
findings.failure_scenario: The compact constructor's comment reads 'Epochs only ever increase, from 0', which after this commit is the direct negation of the invariant the commit exists to establish -- in the record that defines the field and the first file a future author opens. The reservation is enforced by exactly one literal (LeaseManager.java:142) and pinned only through tryAcquire, so a second construction site added later (M4.8's checkpoint pointer, M5's forwarding rebuilding a Lease from decoded bytes) can produce new Lease(0, ...) with nothing failing: LeaseTest itself already constructs new Lease(0, ...) five times, so the record demonstrably accepts it. That lease then feeds new CommitLog(store, prefix, lease.epoch()) and writes straight into the unleased chain -- the exact collision M4.4b closed -- with the whole suite green. The cheapest rung (gate-design rung 1, make the bad state unrepresentable) is available here: refuse epoch 0 in the compact constructor. There is a real argument against it -- decode() would then turn a legacy or hand-edited epoch-0 lease into an IOException, which LeaseManager treats as 'do not take over', trading a liveness stall for the safety -- but the diff neither takes the rung nor records why not.
findings.suggestion: At minimum correct the comment to say epochs start at 1 and 0 is reserved for the unleased chain; ideally refuse 0 in the compact constructor, or say in one line why decode() must keep accepting it.

findings.title: LeaseManager's own class javadoc still says a lost counter restarts at 0
findings.failure_scenario: Ninety lines above the line this commit changed, the class contract still reads 'Deleting it would lose the epoch counter, so the next acquirer would start again at 0 and REUSE an epoch a previous term already wrote objects under'. That is now false: the next acquirer starts at 1. A reader of the class contract concludes cold start is 0 -- the single fact M4.4b changed -- and either reintroduces new Lease(0, ...) or 'corrects' LeaseManager.java:142 back to 0 to match the documentation, reopening the collision. The underlying argument survives verbatim with 1 substituted for 0.
findings.suggestion: s/start again at 0/start again at 1/ and keep the rest of the sentence.

findings.title: Sibling comments and one assertion description still describe the collision as open
findings.failure_scenario: CommitLogTest:247 carries the assertion description 'the no-lease default is epoch 0 -- see M4.4b on why that collides'. An assertion description is what a developer reads at the moment that test fails, and this one now points at a backlog row that says the collision is resolved -- it sends the person debugging to the opposite conclusion. LeaseManagerTest:176 ('the next acquirer would start again at 0'), :301 ('two ingesters on a fresh prefix both holding epoch 0') and StatBlindStore:16 ('both be told they hold epoch 0') are the same staleness: each names 0 where the code now produces 1, in comments that exist specifically to explain why a mutation matters. The assertions themselves are correct; only the prose misleads.
findings.suggestion: Reword CommitLogTest:247 to 'epoch 0 is the reserved no-lease chain (M4.4b)'; substitute 1 for 0 in the three counterfactual comments.

verified.reserving_0_vs_sharing: Reserving is the correct branch of the two the row named. Sharing could only be argued safe if the unleased writers were guaranteed absent, and they are not -- DefaultIngest:135 constructs the 2-arg CommitLog in production. Under sharing, putIfAbsent still gives I1 but a non-leaseholder appends into the leader's chain, so the leader's own recovery folds in offsets it never issued and I3's discarded-suffix clause has no epoch boundary to hang on.
verified.remaining_paths_to_epoch_0: None through LeaseManager. Cold start writes the literal 1 (LeaseManager:142); takeover is Lease.takenOverBy -> epoch+1 with the compact constructor refusing a negative epoch, so it is >= 1; renewedUntil and release preserve the held epoch; held is only ever set in adopt(), from fresh or taken. The unexpired-lease early return leaves held null. The only way a Lease with epoch 0 exists at all is decode() of a hand-edited or legacy object, and such a lease is never adopted -- it is either expired (taken over at 1) or unexpired (tryAcquire returns empty). See F2 for the path that is open outside this class.
verified.collision_closed: Yes for the key space: leased epochs are >= 1, the unleased chain is exactly 0, logPrefix() renders %016x so the prefixes are disjoint strings, and no sequence of acquire/renew/release/takeover produces a shared prefix. What is NOT closed is the consequence -- see F1.
verified.other_dependents_on_first_epoch_0: Searched the tree. No spec, ADR or production code depends on the first term being 0: M4/SPEC.md:460 only requires 'increments by exactly one per acquisition', which still holds, and no ADR states a start value. CommitDelta.java:22 ('M1 writes slot 0 and epoch 0') remains true of the unleased chain. The rest are the stale comments in F2/F3/F4.
verified.test_integrity_trailer: The Test-removed: trailer is the right instrument, and this is not the inversion. The inversion rule 4 catches is an assertion loosened so production can stay wrong; here the direction is verifiable from the diff alone: the specification moved (0 is reserved), the old test's name and its isZero() are unsatisfiable under any correct implementation, and the replacement asserts isEqualTo(1) -- same path, same strength class (both weight 3 in test_integrity.py's table, so nothing was dodged by renaming; the rename raised a louder flag than an in-place edit would have), plus the same holderPodId and expiresAtMillis assertions, plus a new test across both acquisition paths. No coverage was dropped. One caveat: the trailer text should say the test was RENAMED and name its replacement -- a bare 'Test-removed:' in git history reads to a future auditor as coverage deleted.
verified.request_rate: Unchanged and correct. tryAcquire still issues one stat plus one conditional PUT; renew is still one putIfMatch with no re-read; nothing was added to a loop, no LIST was introduced, no idle path issues a request. The reservation adds at most one constant extra key prefix in the store (the unleased chain alongside the leased ones), which scales with nothing. cost.md rules R1-R6 untouched.
verified.unblocks_m45_m46: Partly -- the collision is gone, but 'straight in' is not accurate; see F1.
verified.backlog_row: Accurate on the facts it states and correctly self-reports the gate WARN. Its one overreach is 'M4.5 and M4.6 can now wire lease.epoch() straight in' (F1). 'A new test asserts NO acquisition path ever writes epoch 0' is an example-based proof of a universal, which is conventional here. The 491-count and the RED records are gate territory and not re-checked.
